To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Universe is a dissipative system and that its arrow of time is the result of the interaction with a coarse grained environment, namely the quantum vacuum.

1) the backreaction effect in quantum cosmology is a manifestation of the fluctuation-dissipa- tion theorem relating fluctuations in the quantum fields to the dissipative effect of the fields on the dynamics of the background spacetime, and 2) the backreaction is a source of time-asymmetry in the dynamics of cosmological spacetimes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of quantum field theory and quantum gravity on curved spacetime backgrounds, with a particular focus on the physics of the very early Universe.

the following issues: (1) the role of the quantum vacuum in the dynamics of cosmological models, (2) the relation of quantum fluctuations to dissipations in cosmological dynamics, (3) the relation of fluctuations of quantum fields and dissipation of gravitational energy, (4) the emergence of a time-asymmetry in the Universe, (5) the relation of dissipation to the stability of cosmological structures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Universe is not in a state of equilibrium and that there is a direction of time in the Universe.
the arrow of time is not a fundamental concept in the physical world, but rather an emergent one that arises from the coarse graining of the underlying microscopic laws.
the Universe is not only expanding but also evolving.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the arrow of time is an inevitable consequence of the existence of gravity.

the backreaction of quantum fluctuations can lead to a time-asymmetric behavior of the Universe, which is a necessary condition for the emergence of an arrow of time and of the concept of entropy in the Universe.
